Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Travel & transport

far adverb

a long way

also far away, far off, not far, far from, a long way off

classical

Ov. Ars 2.10: longē quem petō portus abest
Cic. Quinct. 79: quam longē est hinc in saltum Gallicānum? (Lewis & Short)

longē

adverb

far, a long way (off)

With esse and abesse: longē abest, it’s far; nōn longē, not far; longē ā (ab), far from; further is longius (longius nōn discēdam, I won’t go any further: Cic. Fam. 14.2, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quid properās, juvenis? mediīs tua pīnus in undīs nāvigat, et longē quem petō portus abest

    why the hurry, young man? your ship is out in mid-sea, and the harbour I’m making for is far awayOv. Ars 2.9–10

  • 'nihil,' inquit, 'longē est deō'

    ‘nothing,’ she said, ‘is far from God’Aug. Conf. 9.11.28

Other words

  • procul — far off, in the distance, from afar

    adverb · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.15.3: ovēsque sēgregātās ostendit procul; Cic. Cat. 2.29: nōn jam procul, sed hīc praesentēs (Lewis & Short)

    Of what is seen, heard or kept far away: procul hinc, keep away! (Mart. 13.25.1).

  • longinquus, longinqua, longinquum — far-off, distant

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: ex locīs tam longinquīs (Lewis & Short); Tac. Ann. 2.24: ex longinquō

See also far, how far is it?, away, so far so good.
